name: Svatmarama
dates_notes: The author is conventionally placed in the fifteenth century on textual and historical grounds. Biographical evidence is sparse, and the name should not be treated as a securely documented institutional biography.
core_thesis: Svātmārāma is the attributed author of the *Haṭhayogapradīpikā*, a foundational synthesis of premodern Haṭha Yoga. The work organizes bodily postures, breath discipline, seals and locks, and absorptive practice around the transformation and stabilization of vital processes. It presents Haṭha Yoga as a disciplined route toward the goal conventionally called rāja-yoga, while drawing on a wider Śaiva and yogic vocabulary of *prāṇa*, *nāḍī*, *bindu*, and *kuṇḍalinī*. The text is not simply a manual of postures, nor is it reducible to Pātañjala Yoga: its distinctive account of practice gives the body and vital breath an explicitly soteriological role.

engaged_works.title: Hatha-Yoga-Pradipika
engaged_works.composition_dates_notes: Usually assigned to the fifteenth century; a more precise date cannot be securely established.
engaged_works.ascription_notes: The work is consistently transmitted under Svātmārāma's name, but independent biographical evidence for the author is limited.

ascription_evidence.description: Sanskrit manuscript and print transmission presents Svātmārāma as the author.

engaged_works.summary: A four-chapter Sanskrit manual that treats āsana, prāṇāyāma and kumbhaka, mudrā and bandha, and samādhi. It compiles and reorganizes earlier Haṭha Yoga materials rather than offering a biography-linked personal doctrine. Its historical importance is that it became a central textual presentation of Haṭha Yoga's practical and soteriological repertoire.
